cards.title: Rating scale, notchChange and notchCalculator (REQ-06-02) in src/ratings/notch.mjs
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-06-02 is a notch calculator: previous + current rating -> signed notch change, direction, resulting WL (0-4, higher is worse). Other POC parts import this module by exact path and names (fixed contract). T-02 (Indicator 12) builds on notchChange.

REPO FACTS: plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs); package.json has type module and test script 'node --test'. No npm dependencies, runtime or dev. src/ and test/ hold only .gitkeep. Read CLAUDE.md. src/ratings is pure and synchronous: no I/O, no console output. Use no API newer than Node 18 (local runtime is Node 22: take care; no toSorted/toReversed/with, no node:test features added after 18).

FILES: create src/ratings/notch.mjs and the unit test test/ratings/notch.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert/strict).

CONTRACT: (1) export const RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze(["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]) - 19 entries, best first, ASCII hyphen-minus. (2) export function notchChange(previous, current) returns idx(current) - idx(previous), integer -18..18; positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, unchanged 0 and never -0 (do not use -(p - c)). (3) export function notchCalculator(previous, current) returns a NEW plain object with exactly keys { notches, direction, wl }: notches = notchChange(...); direction 'downgrade' if >0, 'upgrade' if <0, 'unchanged' if 0; wl = 2 if notches >= 3, 1 if notches === 2, else 0 (Indicator 13 thresholds, C2/C6). C2: the POC example 'BBB+ -> BB+ = 2 notch -> WL 1' is wrong; it is 3 notches -> WL 2 - cite C2 in the test next to that case. C6: a 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0. Do NOT build a shared threshold helper for Indicator 12 (different thresholds). Each function declares exactly two parameters (previous, current): fn.length === 2; no options/override parameter.

INPUT HANDLING: validate each argument on its own, previous first then current. If typeof value !== 'string' throw RangeError immediately; never coerce (no String(x), no x.trim() on a non-string). null, undefined, missing arg, 5, {}, ['BBB+'], new String('BBB+'), Symbol('BBB+') all throw RangeError, never TypeError. For strings: value.trim() (removes spaces, tabs, newlines, NBSP, NOT U+200B), then toUpperCase(), look up in RATING_SCALE; not found -> RangeError. Inner whitespace is not normalised ('BBB +' rejected); U+2212 minus rejected; 'CC','C','D','NR','Baa1','','   ' rejected. ERROR MESSAGE: names the argument and echoes the value, e.g. Unknown rating for previous: "BB++". Building the echo for a Symbol/object must not throw (template literal with a Symbol throws TypeError: use a safe formatter, JSON.stringify for strings, String(v) or try/catch for others). Tests assert instanceof RangeError, that the message includes the value and names the argument; never the full text.

UNIT TESTS (TDD): scale equality and freeze; notchChange table; trim/case; invalid-input table in both positions for notchChange and notchCalculator; calculator downgrade and upgrade tables; exhaustive 19x19 loop with distribution counts (wl0=208, wl1=17, wl2=136; unchanged=19, downgrade=171, upgrade=171). Use assert.strictEqual (Object.is catches -0). Stdout/stderr silence: temporarily wrap process.stdout.write/process.stderr.write during calls, then restore.
acceptance: AC-1 [P0] (wrong scale = every notch miscounted): Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from "./src/ratings/notch.mjs"`, when it is read, then `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"])`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, `RATING_SCALE[0] === "AAA"`, `RATING_SCALE[18] === "CCC-"`, and no entry contains U+2212 (only ASCII `-` U+002D).

AC-2 [P2]: Given `RATING_SCALE`, when a consumer tries to change it, then `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`, `RATING_SCALE.push("D")` throws `TypeError`, and `RATING_SCALE[0] = "X"` (strict-mode ESM test file) throws `TypeError`. Afterwards `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, `RATING_SCALE[0] === "AAA"` and `notchChange("AAA","AA+") === 1`.

AC-3 [P0] (wrong sign turns a downgrade into an upgrade): Given two valid ratings, when `notchChange(previous, current)` is called, then it returns `index(current) − index(previous)`: `("BBB+","BB+") → 3`, `("BBB+","BBB-") → 2`, `("BBB+","BBB") → 1`, `("BB+","BBB+") → -3`, `("AAA","CCC-") → 18`, `("CCC-","AAA") → -18`, `("A","A") → 0`. `Number.isInteger(result)` holds for each.
AC-3 [P0]: Given any rating `r` in `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchChange(r, r)` is called, then `Object.is(result, 0) === true` (never `-0`; `assert.strictEqual(result, 0)`).

AC-4 [P1] (padded or lower-case input rejected; workaround: the caller normalises it): Given ratings that differ from the canonical form only by case or leading/trailing whitespace, when `notchChange` gets them in either position, then the result equals the canonical result: `("bbb+","BB+") → 3`, `("  BBB+ ","bb+") → 3`, `("\tBbb+\n","BB+") → 3`, `(" BBB+ ","BB+") → 3`.
AC-4 [P1]: Given `notchCalculator(" bbb+","bbb- ")`, when it is called, then the result deep-equals `{ notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`.

AC-5 [P1] (bad code gives a wrong WL or NaN; workaround: pick only from `RATING_SCALE`): Given each invalid value `v` from the Test data invalid table, when `notchChange(v,"BBB")`, `notchChange("BBB",v)`, `notchCalculator(v,"BBB")` and `notchCalculator("BBB",v)` are called, then each throws an error with `err instanceof RangeError` and `!(err instanceof TypeError)`, and no value is returned. `notchChange("BBB")` and `notchCalculator("BBB")` (second argument missing) also throw `RangeError`.

AC-5 [P1]: Given exactly one bad argument, when it is called, then validation is per argument: `notchChange("BBB+","CC")` and `notchChange("CC","BBB+")` both throw `RangeError`. When both are bad, `notchChange("CC","DD")` throws a `RangeError` that names `previous` (previous is checked first, per the card contract).

AC-5 [P1]: Given an invalid string, when it is thrown, then the message names the argument and contains the received value. `notchChange("BB++","BBB")` has a message that includes `BB++` and `previous`. `notchChange("BBB","BB++")` has a message that includes `BB++` and `current`. `notchCalculator` behaves the same. Tests assert only these substrings, never the full text.

AC-5 [P1]: Given a non-string, when it is passed, then it is not coerced. `["BBB+"]`, `new String("BBB+")` and `{ toString() { return "BBB+"; } }` each throw `RangeError` in either position. `Symbol("BBB+")`, `null` and `undefined` throw `RangeError`, never a `TypeError` from `trim`, from building the message or from a template literal.

AC-6 [P0] (wrong threshold misrates the client): Given a downgrade, when `notchCalculator(previous, current)` is called, then it returns: `("BBB+","BB+") → { notches: 3, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }` (the test cites C2 here: the POC example "2 notch → WL=1" is wrong); `("BBB+","BBB-") → { notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`; `("BBB+","BBB") → { notches: 1, direction: "downgrade", wl: 0 }` (C6); `("BBB-","BB") → { notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`; `("BBB-","BB-") → { notches: 3, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }`; `("AAA","CCC-") → { notches: 18, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }`.

AC-7 [P0] (a WL on an upgrade puts a healthy client on the watchlist): Given an upgrade or an unchanged rating, when `notchCalculator` is called, then it returns: `("BBB","BBB+") → { notches: -1, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }`; `("BBB-","BBB+") → { notches: -2, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }` (catches a `Math.abs` threshold); `("BB+","BBB+") → { notches: -3, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }`; `("CCC-","AAA") → { notches: -18, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }`; `("A","A") → { notches: 0, direction: "unchanged", wl: 0 }`, with `Object.is(result.notches, 0)`.

AC-8 [P1] (screens break if the shape drifts; few consumers yet): Given each of the 361 pairs `(p, c)` of `RATING_SCALE × RATING_SCALE`, when `notchCalculator(p, c)` is called, then `Object.keys(r).sort()` deep-equals `["direction","notches","wl"]`; `r.notches === notchChange(p, c)`; `direction` is `"downgrade"` / `"upgrade"` / `"unchanged"` for notches > 0 / < 0 / = 0; `wl` is `2` for notches ≥ 3, `1` for notches = 2, and `0` otherwise; totals: wl 0 = 208, wl 1 = 17, wl 2 = 136; unchanged = 19, downgrade = 171, upgrade = 171.

AC-8 [P1]: Given two calls `a = notchCalculator("BBB+","BB+")` and `b = notchCalculator("BBB+","BB+")`, when they are compared, then `a !== b`, `Object.getPrototypeOf(a) === Object.prototype`, and setting `a.wl = 0` leaves `b.wl === 2` and a third call's `wl === 2`.

AC-12 [P1] (a rename breaks the importing POC parts): Given `import * as ns from "./src/ratings/notch.mjs"`, when it is inspected, then `ns.RATING_SCALE` is an array, `typeof ns.notchChange === "function"`, `typeof ns.notchCalculator === "function"`, `notchChange.length === 2` and `notchCalculator.length === 2`. No override parameter exists (C7): `notchCalculator("BBB+","BB+",{ wl: 0 }).wl === 2`.

AC-12 [P1]: Given `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write` wrapped to count calls, when all 361 pairs go through both functions and the invalid table is run, then both counts are `0`. The originals are restored afterwards, in a `finally` block.

cards.title: Indicator 12 country rating change WL (REQ-03-12) in src/indicators/countryRating.mjs
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-03-12 is Indicator 12, the country rating change. It maps a country rating move to a WL (higher is worse) that feeds the client's WL directly. Other POC parts import this module by exact path and name. It must be built on the shared notch count from T-01 (merged before this card starts).

REPO FACTS: plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs); no npm dependencies, runtime or dev. src/indicators is pure and synchronous: no I/O, no console output. No API newer than Node 18 (local runtime is Node 22: take care). Read CLAUDE.md. Tests use node:test + node:assert/strict.

FILES: create src/indicators/countryRating.mjs and the unit test test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs. Do not modify src/ratings/** (T-01's scope); report a defect there rather than editing.

CONTRACT: export function countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current): exactly two parameters (fn.length === 2), no options/override parameter. Returns the number 2 when notches >= 2, 1 when notches === 1, else 0, where notches = notchChange(previous, current). Must `import { notchChange } from '../ratings/notch.mjs'` and must NOT keep its own scale, rating list or validation. Upgrade/unchanged -> 0. IMPORTANT: Indicator 12 maps 1 notch -> WL 1 and 2+ -> WL 2, while notchCalculator maps 1 -> 0, 2 -> 1, 3+ -> 2. Do not share a threshold helper. Add a test for BBB+ -> BBB showing Indicator 12 gives 1 while notchCalculator(...).wl gives 0.

INPUT HANDLING: inherited from notchChange (trim, case-insensitive, each argument validated separately, non-strings never coerced, anything outside the 19-rating scale -> RangeError never TypeError, message names the argument and echoes the value, e.g. Unknown rating for previous: "BB++"). Pass arguments straight to notchChange(previous, current); do not wrap, catch or rethrow.

UNIT TESTS (TDD): downgrade table; upgrade/unchanged table; trim/case; invalid-input table in both positions ('', '   ', 'BBB +', 'BB++', 'CC', 'C', 'D', 'NR', 'Baa1', 'BBB\u2212', '\u200BBBB+', null, undefined, missing 2nd arg, 5, {}, ['BBB+'], Symbol('BBB+')); exhaustive 19x19 loop over RATING_SCALE against notchChange with counts 0=190, 1=18, 2=153. Stdout/stderr silence by temporarily wrapping process.stdout.write/process.stderr.write. As the last card, confirm `npm test` from the worktree root runs both test files and exits 0.
acceptance: AC-9 [P0] (wrong threshold misclassifies the client): Given a country downgrade, when `countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current)` is called, then 1 notch → `1`: `("BBB+","BBB") → 1`, `("BBB-","BB+") → 1`, `("AAA","AA+") → 1`, `("CCC","CCC-") → 1`; 2 or more notches → `2`: `("BBB+","BBB-") → 2`, `("A","BBB+") → 2`, `("BBB+","BB+") → 2` (3 notches), `("CCC+","CCC-") → 2`, `("AAA","CCC-") → 2` (18 notches).

AC-9 [P0]: Given any valid pair, when the function returns, then `typeof result === "number"`, `Number.isInteger(result)`, and `[0,1,2].includes(result)`. It never returns a string, a boolean or an object.

AC-10 [P0] (a flagged upgrade raises a false watchlist alert): Given an upgrade or an unchanged rating, when the function is called, then it returns `0`: `("BBB","BBB+")`, `("BBB-","BBB+")` (−2, catches a `Math.abs` threshold), `("BB+","BBB+")`, `("AA+","AAA")`, `("CCC-","AAA")`, `("A","A")`; and for every `r` in `RATING_SCALE`, `Object.is(countryRatingChangeWl(r, r), 0)`.

AC-11 [P1] (the indicators disagree on the same move; workaround: a manual recount): Given the same pair, when Indicator 12 and the calculator are compared, then the two threshold sets differ as the business confirmed: `("BBB+","BBB")`: `countryRatingChangeWl` is `1`, `notchCalculator(...).wl` is `0`; `("BBB+","BBB-")`: `2` vs `1`; `("BBB+","BB+")`: `2` vs `2`.

AC-11 [P1]: Given each of the 361 pairs of `RATING_SCALE × RATING_SCALE`, when `countryRatingChangeWl(p, c)` is called, then it equals `2` if `notchChange(p,c) ≥ 2`, `1` if it is `1`, and `0` otherwise. Totals: `0` = 190, `1` = 18, `2` = 153.

AC-11 [P1]: Given `src/indicators/countryRating.mjs`, when it is reviewed, then it contains `import { notchChange } from "../ratings/notch.mjs"`, has no rating list or scale of its own and no validation of its own, and has no `try`/`catch` around `notchChange` and no shared threshold helper with `notchCalculator`.

AC-4 [P1]: Given input that differs from the canonical form only by case or leading/trailing whitespace, when the function gets it in either position, then `("a","  bbb+ ") → 2`, `("bbb+","bbb") → 1`, `("\tBBB+\n","BB+") → 2`, `(" bbb-","bb+ ") → 1`.

AC-5 [P1] (a bad code gives a wrong WL; workaround: pick only from `RATING_SCALE`): Given each invalid value `v` from the Test data invalid table, when `countryRatingChangeWl(v,"BBB")` and `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB",v)` are called, then each throws with `err instanceof RangeError` and `!(err instanceof TypeError)`. `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB")` (second argument missing) throws `RangeError`. `("BBB+","CC")` and `("CC","BBB+")` both throw.

AC-5 [P1]: Given an invalid string, when it is thrown, then the error is the one `notchChange` raises, passed through unchanged: `countryRatingChangeWl("BB++","BBB")` throws a `RangeError` whose message includes `BB++` and `previous`, and equals the message of `notchChange("BB++","BBB")`; `("BBB","BB++")` includes `BB++` and `current`; non-strings (`["BBB+"]`, `new String("BBB+")`, `Symbol("BBB+")`, `null`) are never coerced and never raise `TypeError`.

AC-12 [P1] (a rename breaks the importing POC parts): Given `import * as ns from "./src/indicators/countryRating.mjs"`, when it is inspected, then `typeof ns.countryRatingChangeWl === "function"` and `countryRatingChangeWl.length === 2`; a third argument has no effect: `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB+","BBB",{ wl: 0 }) === 1` (C7); with `process.stdout.write`/`process.stderr.write` wrapped across all 361 pairs and the invalid table, both write counts are `0` (originals restored in a `finally` block).

AC-13 [P2]: Given the T-02 worktree with T-01 merged, when `npm test` runs from the worktree root, then it exits `0`, its output shows tests from both `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and `test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs` with `# fail 0`, and `package.json` has no `dependencies` and no `devDependencies` key.

cards.title: Fix F-1: restore C1 RATING_SCALE order (BBB- before BB+) in src/ratings/notch.mjs on the job branch
cards.context:
WHY: Finding F-1. T-01 (REQ-06-02 notch calculator) passed gate, QA and review on its card branch with the correct scale. After 'dl integrate T-01', the job branch head is 50dcb5e 'refactor: tidy the rating scale', which swapped two adjacent entries of RATING_SCALE in src/ratings/notch.mjs. On the job branch the scale reads ... "BBB", "BB+", "BBB-", "BB" ... where it should read ... "BBB", "BBB-", "BB+", "BB" .... Every notch count crossing that boundary is wrong (e.g. BBB+ -> BB+ gives 2 notches/WL 1 instead of 3 notches/WL 2). The merged-suite run fails AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-6, AC-7 of the QA integration tests; the unit test already pins the order with EXPECTED_SCALE. The origin of 50dcb5e is unknown. Do not revert or rewrite history: make a normal forward commit on your card branch, which starts from the job branch (the merged state), not main.

REPO FACTS: plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs). No npm dependencies. Read CLAUDE.md. src/ratings is pure and synchronous: no I/O, no console output. No API newer than Node 18.

FILES: src/ratings/notch.mjs (only the RATING_SCALE literal) and test/ratings/notch.test.mjs (add regression tests only; never loosen or remove an existing test). Do not touch src/indicators/** or test/integration/**.

CONTRACT (unchanged): export const RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze(["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]); 19 entries, ASCII hyphen only, frozen. Index 9 is "BBB-", index 10 is "BB+". notchChange, notchCalculator, validation and messages do not change.

REGRESSION TESTS (TDD: write first, watch them fail, then fix): in test/ratings/notch.test.mjs add a test named for F-1 / scale order asserting RATING_SCALE.indexOf("BBB-")===9, indexOf("BB+")===10, every adjacent pair of the literal expected list has notchChange 1 (against the literal list, not derived from RATING_SCALE), notchChange("BBB","BBB-")===1, ("BBB-","BB+")===1, ("BBB","BB+")===2, and notchCalculator("BBB+","BB+") deep-equals {notches:3,direction:"downgrade",wl:2} (C2). Keep the existing AC-1 deepStrictEqual test and the 19x19 distribution counts (wl0=208, wl1=17, wl2=136). Extend notch.test.mjs; no new test file.

NOTE: T-02 (Indicator 12) imports notchChange from this module; its expected values are only right after this fix.
acceptance: AC-1 [P0] (a wrong scale miscounts every notch across BBB-/BB+ and misrates the client): Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from "./src/ratings/notch.mjs"` on the card branch (based on job branch head 50dcb5e), when it is read, then `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"])` passes, `RATING_SCALE.indexOf("BBB") === 8`, `RATING_SCALE[9] === "BBB-"`, `RATING_SCALE[10] === "BB+"`, `RATING_SCALE.indexOf("BB") === 11`, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19`, `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`, and every entry matches `/^[A-Z+-]+$/` (no U+2212, no U+2013).

AC-1 [P0]: Given the card branch, when `git rev-parse HEAD:src/ratings/notch.mjs` runs, then it prints `8f151881853664b44568be558d7f8aac0cd874c1` (the blob of gated card commit 8a1309d), so `git diff 8a1309d HEAD -- src/ratings/notch.mjs` is empty.

AC-3 [P0] (a wrong count or sign makes the WL wrong): Given the corrected scale, when `notchChange` is called, then `("BBB","BBB-") → 1`, `("BBB-","BB+") → 1`, `("BBB","BB+") → 2`, `("BBB+","BB+") → 3`, `("BBB+","BBB-") → 2`, `("BB+","BBB+") → -3`, `("BBB-","BBB") → -1`, `("bbb-"," bb+ ") → 1`; and for each i in 0..17, `notchChange(EXPECTED[i], EXPECTED[i+1]) === 1` and the reverse `=== -1`, where EXPECTED is the literal C1 list written out in the test (not built from `RATING_SCALE`).
